# 3 Resampling & Alignment

Time series often come at different sampling rates or
need to be transformed to a different time scale.

Common reasons:

-   Comparing two time series
-   Reducing noise through aggregation
-   Adjusting to reporting intervals
-   Preparing for modeling

------------------------------------------------------------------------

::: {.callout-note title="Note"}
Resampling means changing the time scale. You must decide
between aggregation and interpolation.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.1 Original Time Series (Hourly)

::: {#5455a3e8 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(2)

t = pd.date_range("2025-01-01", periods=24*5, freq="h")
y = pd.Series(10 + rng.normal(size=len(t)), index=t, name="signal")

y.plot(title="Hourly Time Series")
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](03-resampling-alignment_files/figure-html/cell-2-output-1.png){width=566 height=461}
:::
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.2 Downsampling (Aggregation)

We aggregate from hours to days.

::: {#af919df0 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
daily_mean = y.resample("D").mean()
daily_max = y.resample("D").max()

ax = daily_mean.plot(marker="o", label="Daily Mean")
daily_max.plot(ax=ax, marker="o", label="Daily Maximum")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Downsampling: Hours → Days")
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](03-resampling-alignment_files/figure-html/cell-3-output-1.png){width=587 height=461}
:::
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

::: {.callout-tip title="Decision Guide"}
-   Mean → smooths out fluctuations\
-   Maximum → highlights extreme values\
-   Sum → useful for quantities (e.g., energy consumption)
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.3 Upsampling (Interpolation)

We increase the temporal resolution.

::: {#86e44e1e .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
y_2h = y.resample("2h").mean()
y_up = y_2h.resample("h").interpolate("time")

ax = y_2h.plot(marker="o", label="2H (aggregated)")
y_up.plot(ax=ax, alpha=0.7, label="Interpolated to 1H")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Upsampling with Interpolation")
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](03-resampling-alignment_files/figure-html/cell-4-output-1.png){width=579 height=461}
:::
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

::: {.callout-warning title="Warning"}
Interpolation does not generate new measurement data; it only models
a plausible progression.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.4 Alignment of Two Time Series

Two time series with different sampling rates:

::: {#b04eccb5 .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
t2 = pd.date_range("2025-01-01", periods=24*5, freq="2h")
y2 = pd.Series(5 + rng.normal(size=len(t2)), index=t2, name="signal2")
```
:::


For joint analysis, both series must have the same frequency.

::: {#bb3e15e1 .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
y2_aligned = y2.resample("h").interpolate("time")

df = pd.concat([y, y2_aligned], axis=1)

df.plot(title="Aligned Time Series")
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](03-resampling-alignment_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){width=566 height=461}
:::
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

::: {.callout-note title="Note"}
Alignment means: - same frequency - same time span - same
time zone
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.5 Common Sources of Error

-   Comparisons without prior resampling
-   Mixing local time and UTC
-   Aggregation without considering data types (e.g., sum vs
    mean)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.6 Mini Exercise

1.  Generate a minute-level time series over 2 days.
2.  Aggregate to hourly averages.
3.  Compare visually:
    -   Original
    -   Hourly averages
4.  Interpret the loss of information.
